findings.title: `--estimate` reports BUY for any non-"nothing_to_buy" verdict, including refusals
findings.description: When `check_ceilings=False`, `judge_estimate` returns `Estimate.BUY` immediately after the scope check. It returns before the later `summary["verdict"] != VERDICT_ALLOWED` branch, so that branch never runs in this mode. A verdict of `refused` for a reason other than the ceilings (for example, a provider or planner refusal) is therefore reported as BUY. `_estimate_only` then prints `verdict refused: Estimate.BUY` and the PM's ceiling command. The test `test_estimate_prints_the_command_and_buys_nothing` only exercises a `refused` verdict whose reason is "ceiling", so it hides this. Skipping only the ceiling comparisons would be correct, but the verdict check should still run, or `--estimate` should print the verdict reasons.

findings.title: Naive and aware datetimes can be compared in resubmit matching
findings.description: `resubmit_origins` parses `requested_at` with `datetime.fromisoformat`. `judge()` in `cutover_304_first_purchase.py` parses `start`, which is tz-aware. If the `debug requests` JSON renders `requested_at` without an offset, `made < since` in `_check_resubmit` raises a raw `TypeError`. It would not raise a `CutoverError`, and the operator would see an unexplained crash. The tests only use `+00:00` values, so nothing covers the naive case. `_edge_of` already rejects naive instants explicitly, and this path should do the same, or a test should pin the real CLI's format.

findings.title: Untyped `origins = {}` under the strict pyright requirement
findings.description: `origins = {}` has no annotation, which strict pyright reports as an unknown type. Annotate it as `dict[RequestKey, datetime]`. Separately, `_check_scope` reuses the loop name `key` for a different type, and a distinct name would read better.

findings.title: Tests duplicate the universe-entry construction
findings.description: `test_coverage_reads_derive_from_the_universe` and `test_an_open_ended_want_is_a_stop_not_a_default` build `TickUniverseEntry` objects by chaining `.__class__` on existing instances. This is hard to read and repeats code. Import `TickUniverseEntry` and `HistoryWant` directly, or add a shared fixture.

findings.title: Fail-explicit design and test coverage for the new verdict modules
findings.description: The new modules raise `CutoverError` with distinct messages instead of falling back to defaults. The gate, edge and exit-rule checks each have targeted tests, including edge cases such as an equal edge, a naive instant, unknown buckets and a missing key. `purchase_verdicts.py` stays under the ~300-line limit. The try/except blocks are narrow and re-raise with `from exc`. The tests build fixtures from the real CLI renderers (`_cell`, `_product_payload`, `coverage_to_dict`), which follows the project's parser-fixture rule.

structured_findings.summary: `--estimate` reports BUY for any non-"nothing_to_buy" verdict, including refusals
Naive and aware datetimes can be compared in resubmit matching
Untyped `origins = {}` under the strict pyright requirement
Fail-explicit design and test coverage for the new verdict modules
